concerns.text: FR-001 requires loading *public RCT datasets* with genuine treatment and outcome variables, but the plan later states that no verified RCT datasets exist and that treatment/outcome columns will be synthesized from non‑RCT observational data. This directly contradicts the functional requirement.

Cross‑references to “US-1”, “US-2”, “US-3” are used throughout the FR and SC sections, yet the user stories are labeled “User Story 1”, “User Story 2”, etc. The terminology is unstable and may cause confusion in traceability.

FR-005 states that Complete‑Case analysis uses “t‑test/Wilcoxon”. However FR-007 mandates that for binary outcomes the system must use a logistic‑based or other non‑parametric test instead of a t‑test, and Wilcoxon is not appropriate for binary data. The two requirements conflict on the allowed test for binary outcomes.

FR-006 prescribes a Binomial test to assess deviation of the empirical Type I error rate from the nominal 0.05 level. SC-005, however, proposes using a Binomial test to compare two estimated error rates (error_CC > 2·error_MI), which is a different statistical question and contradicts the intended use of the Binomial test.

The phrase “(See US-1)” appears in multiple FRs, but there is no artifact labeled US‑1; the only related sections are the “User Story” blocks. This broken cross‑reference should be corrected to point to the appropriate user story identifier.

The overall claim is to assess validity in *Randomized Controlled Trials*, yet the data acquisition strategy relies on non‑RCT observational datasets with synthetic treatment variables. This scope shift is not reconciled with the stated research focus and violates the consistency between the problem statement and the data source requirement.
